evals.prompt:
Review this pro-gated affordance in the editor. Instead of the shared component, the custom survey URL feature is gated with a hand-rolled modal: `

This is a Pro feature. Upgrade to unlock it.

`.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: C1 — gated affordance must use the shared Paywall component (or PaywallCrownBadge, or the crown beside its own button), not a bespoke modal/tooltip/popover
evals.expected_output: C1 FAILs. The upgrade prompt is a bespoke <Modal> with a "See plans" button rather than the shared <Paywall> component, so it drifts from the presenter app's UpgradePopover and breaks the single-source-of-truth contract (PAYWALL-01). Fix: wrap the gated field in <Paywall featureKey="custom_survey_url" featureLabel="Custom survey URL" body="Give your survey a branded, memorable link." requiredPlan="pro"> and delete the bespoke modal. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Cites a hand-rolled Modal instead of the shared Paywall component

evals.prompt:
Review this paywall popover markup: `

Custom survey URL is a premium feature and gives you a branded link plus more control…

Maybe later`. It uses the Phosphor Crown glyph, a multi-line body, hand-rolled antd buttons instead of the shared , and an extra 'Maybe later' dismiss link.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: C2 — popover anatomy: crown mark (custom, not Phosphor) + label + one-sentence body + unlock line + exactly the two shared CTAs (Upgrade positive, See all plans secondary), nothing more
evals.expected_output: C2 FAILs. The popover anatomy is wrong: it uses the generic Phosphor <Crown /> instead of the custom Vivid Pink CrownBadge, the body runs longer than one sentence, the unlock line is missing, the two CTAs are hand-rolled antd <Button>s rather than the shared <aha-button> (Upgrade positive + See all plans secondary), and it adds a banned 'Maybe later' dismiss link. Fix: use the shared <aha-paywall> popover — crown mark + short feature label, a one-sentence value prop, the unlock line, then exactly the two shared CTAs, with no dismiss link (PAYWALL-02/-03/-04). Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Cites Phosphor Crown instead of the custom CrownBadge
Cites the extra dismiss link, hand-rolled buttons and/or multi-sentence body / missing unlock line

evals.prompt: Review this paywall props contract: `<Paywall featureKey="Results Export" featureLabel="Export results" body="Download every response as a CSV." requiredPlan="premium" />`. featureKey is Title Case with a space and requiredPlan is 'premium'.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: C3 — props contract: featureKey stable snake_case, requiredPlan one of essential|pro
evals.expected_output: C3 FAILs. The props contract is violated: featureKey "Results Export" is Title Case with a space rather than a stable snake_case token, and requiredPlan="premium" is not a real tier (must be essential | pro) (PAYWALL-05/-07). Fix: set featureKey="results_export" (snake_case, reused across analytics and DOM hooks) and requiredPlan="essential" (or "pro"). Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Cites requiredPlan not being a real tier (essential|pro)

evals.prompt: Review this paywall copy: featureLabel is "Unlock a custom URL for your survey now!", body is "This is a Pro feature.", and the CTA label is "Go Pro".
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: C4 — copy rules: noun-phrase label, one benefit sentence body, fixed unlock line, verb 'Upgrade' CTA
evals.expected_output: C4 FAILs. The copy breaks every rule: the feature label is a CTA-style sentence instead of a short noun phrase, the body names the tier ("This is a Pro feature.") instead of describing the one-sentence benefit of unlocking, and the CTA "Go Pro" is not the verb "Upgrade" without a clear reason. Fix: label a noun phrase like "Custom survey URL"; body one benefit sentence ending in a period, e.g. "Give your survey a branded, memorable link."; keep the fixed unlock line verbatim; CTA "Upgrade". Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Cites body naming the tier instead of the benefit and/or the non-verb CTA

evals.prompt: Review this paywall CTA handler: `const onCta = () => { openUpgradeUrl(); track('upgrade_clicked'); };`. There is also no PAYWALL_SHOWN event fired when the popover opens.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: C5 — analytics: PAYWALL_SHOWN on open + PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED before navigation, each with { feature, plan }
evals.expected_output: C5 FAILs. The analytics contract is not wired: there is no PAYWALL_SHOWN on open, the click event is named 'upgrade_clicked' (not PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED) with no { feature, plan } props, and it fires after navigation instead of before. Fix: fire PAYWALL_SHOWN with { feature: featureKey, plan: requiredPlan } when the popover opens, and in the handler call track('PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED', { feature: featureKey, plan: requiredPlan }) BEFORE openUpgradeUrl()/onUpgrade() (PAYWALL-06). Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Cites renamed/mis-propped event and/or click firing after navigation

evals.prompt: Review this default paywall Upgrade handler: `const onCta = () => { window.location.href = UPGRADE_URL; };`. It navigates in the same tab, does not close the popover, and when an onUpgrade prop is provided it is ignored.
evals.label: bad-example
evals.notes: C6 — upgrade URL/handler: open UPGRADE_URL in a new tab with noopener,noreferrer, close popover, honour onUpgrade
evals.expected_output: C6 FAILs. The upgrade handler navigates in the same tab via window.location.href with no noopener,noreferrer, never closes the popover, and ignores the provided onUpgrade prop. Fix: for the default path call window.open(UPGRADE_URL, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer') then close the popover; when onUpgrade is provided, run it instead (analytics still fires first) and still close the popover. Overall: NEEDS FIX.
assertions: Cites popover not closing and/or onUpgrade ignored

evals.prompt: Review this pro-gated custom survey URL field. `<Paywall featureKey="custom_survey_url" featureLabel="Custom survey URL" body="Give your survey a branded, memorable link." requiredPlan="pro"><UrlField disabled /></Paywall>`. The popover renders the purple-circle CrownBadge + "Custom survey URL", the one-sentence body, the line "Unlock with the pro plan." (plan bold), and the two shared <aha-button> CTAs, a positive "Upgrade" and a secondary "See all plans". On open it fires track('PAYWALL_SHOWN', { feature: 'custom_survey_url', plan: 'pro' }); the CTA handler is `const onCta = () => { track('PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED', { feature: 'custom_survey_url', plan: 'pro' }); onUpgrade ? onUpgrade() : window.open(UPGRADE_URL, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer'); close(); };`. The field has a natural anchor so no crown-badge-only anchor is needed.
evals.label: good-control
evals.notes: Good control — a correct Paywall; every applicable criterion passes, C7 N/A (feature has a natural anchor)
evals.expected_output: All applicable criteria PASS. C1: routes through the shared <Paywall> component. C2: correct anatomy — custom CrownBadge + short label, one-sentence body, "Unlock with the <Plan> plan." line, and exactly the two shared CTAs, Upgrade (positive) and See all plans (secondary). C3: featureKey is snake_case and requiredPlan is a real tier (pro). C4: noun-phrase label, one benefit-sentence body, verb CTA "Upgrade". C5: PAYWALL_SHOWN on open and PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED before navigation, each with { feature, plan }. C6: default CTA opens UPGRADE_URL in a new tab with noopener,noreferrer, honours onUpgrade, and closes the popover. C7 is N/A — the field has its own natural anchor. Overall: OK TO SHIP.
assertions: Overall verdict is OK TO SHIP
C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 are all marked PASS

evals.prompt: Review this plan-gated export button that keeps its own place in a card's footer. `<button id="export">Export</button> <aha-paywall feature-key="export_pdf" feature-label="Export to PDF" body="Keep a copy of every slide to share after the session." required-plan="pro"></aha-paywall>` with `button.addEventListener('click', (event) => toggleLockedPaywall(crown, event))`. It fires PAYWALL_SHOWN on open and PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED before navigation.

evals.notes: Good control — a crown beside its own button routes through the shared Paywall; C1 passes, C7 N/A (the feature has a natural anchor)
evals.expected_output: All applicable criteria PASS. C1: the button keeps its own place and the crown sits beside it, with the click routed to the same popover through toggleLockedPaywall, so there is no bespoke upsell. C7 is N/A: the feature has a natural anchor. Overall: OK TO SHIP.
